teaching: Kitab al-Mabda' wa'l-Ma'ad by Sayyidna Mu'ayyad is the first book ever written on the subject of origin and return (mabda' wa'l-ma'ad), belonging to the Tayyibi haqa'iq tradition.
Sayyidna Mu'ayyad's famous couplet declares that had he lived in the time of the Prophet Muhammad, his rank would not have been less than that of Salman.
Sayyidna Mu'ayyad authored 800 majalis (sermons) that encompass all the religious sciences.
Sayyidna Mu'ayyad held a very high rank among the bab al-abwab (gate of gates) of the da'wah.
Imam Mustansir gave Sayyidna Mu'ayyad the rank of abu'd-du'at (father of the du'at), to lead the prayers of the du'at; the umm al-du'at (mother of the du'at) is Arwa bint Ahmad, Hurrat al-Malika.
When the a'immah went into concealment, the du'at took over the representation of the Imams; Sayyidna Zu'ayb bin Musa was appointed the first da'i by Mu'ayyad and Hurrat al-Malika.
The prayer of the second day uniquely takes its wasila from the muqatta' Kaf Ha Ya 'Ayn Sad, a non-repeating (ghayr-i mukarrar) disjointed-letter group occurring only once in the Quran.

Kaf Ha Ya 'Ayn Sad is interpreted as: with Kaf You sufficed (kafayta), with Ha You guided (hadayta), with Ya You made easy (yassarta), with 'Ayn You forgave ('afawta), with Sad You spoke the truth (sadaqta).
Allah has the power to forgive all sins (inna-llaha yaghfiru'dh-dhunuba jami'a).
The Prophet was known as al-Sadiq al-Amin (the truthful, the trustworthy); at the warning of his nearest kindred he presented his hujjat (proof) before announcing his nubuwwat and risalat.
There are two pivotal days in the history of Islam: yawm 'ashirat al-aqrabin (the day of warning the nearest kindred) and the Day of Ghadir.

At the gathering of the kindred, the ten-year-old Ali was the first to say 'Ya Rasulullah' and pledge support; the Prophet declared that whoever supported him would be his khalifa, wasi, and janishin.
On the Day of Ghadir the verse al-yawma akmaltu lakum dinakum was revealed and the Prophet declared man kuntu mawlahu fa-hadha 'aliyyun mawlahu (of whomsoever I am the master, Ali is his master).
Al-Mu'ayyad was a title given by Imam Mustansir (the 18th Imam); his original name was Hibatullah bin Musa bin Sulayman bin Adam al-Shirazi, and his father too was a da'i.
Sayyidna Mu'ayyad was from Shiraz in Iran and later came to Misr (Egypt), where the a'immah and the da'wah were located at that time.
Mufarrij al-Abwab by Sayyidna Ali bin Sulayman is a magnificently arranged collection of the authentic (mustanad) prayers of the Ahl al-Bayt, the Prophet, and Ali.
Sayyidna Mu'ayyad fi'l-Din was from the progeny of the Prophet Sulayman bin Dawud.
Only two prophets passed from mustawda' (temporary abode) to mustaqarr (permanent abode): Idris (of whom it is said wa-rafa'nahu makanan 'aliyya) and Sulayman.

After Sayyidna Muhammad bin Isma'il, the Imams went into concealment; the three concealed Imams (al-masturin al-thalatha) are Ya'la, Ali, and Abu Talib Ali, whose veils (hujub) are 'Abdullah, Ahmad, and Husayn.
In the time of Mawlana Ahmad existed the Rasa'il of the Ikhwan al-Safa.
Sayyidna Mu'ayyad was the hujjat al-'uzma before Imam Mustansir and had many compositions in the zahir, the batin, and the haqa'iq.
Sayyidna Mu'ayyad passed away in the last ten days of Shawwal in 470 Hijri and was buried in the Dar al-'Ilm in al-Qahira al-Mu'izziyya in Egypt.

Mu'ayyad's maternal uncle kept him from the Imam for five years; when he finally reached the Imam he received gnosis and high ranks, and the Imam wrote that if Mu'ayyad's hands were cut off no other Mu'ayyad would be found.
The haqa'iq of Sayyidna Mu'ayyad's du'as were written by Sayyidna Isma'il ibn Muhammad (the Da'i Shumukh) in Kitab al-Subuh; he also authored Mansak al-Hajj.

The book's opening khutba praises Allah, Lord of the worlds, and sends blessings on the Messenger Muhammad the seal of the prophets, his legatee Ali ibn Abi Talib the noblest of legatees, and the Imams of their pure progeny.
Allah described Himself as rabbu'l-'alamin (Lord of the worlds) rather than khaliqu'l-'alamin (creator) because tarbiyat (nurturing) is a higher rank than creation.
The importance of parents derives not from giving birth but from being responsible for upbringing (tarbiyat).
For whichever world Allah is the Lord, the Prophet is its mercy (rahmatan li'l-'alamin).
Allah gave the Messenger such eminence that He made him a partner with Himself in seeing and deciding the deeds of all people (sayara-llahu a'malakum wa-rasuluhu).
Allah, the Knower of the unseen and witnessed ('Alim al-ghaybi wa'sh-shahadah), discloses His unseen to no one except a messenger whom He has chosen (illa man irtada min rasul, Surah al-Jinn).
Allah's pleasure with the Messenger is mentioned in Surah al-Duha (fa-tarda), promising he will be given until he is satisfied.
The Quran from beginning to end is like a qasidah (ode) in praise of the Messenger.
Janab Zaynab taught the haqa'iq of Kaf Ha Ya 'Ayn Sad to women; Sayyidna Sulayman bin Hasan (Wawaam) will manifest as Mawlatuna Zaynab in the next raj'at.
The treatise is addressed to a pious, rightly-guided brother and answers his question about attaining success and felicity in the ma'ad (hereafter).

The secret of the spiritual malakut connects through revelation with every spiritual rank and reaches the hudud of the sincere ones (mukhlisin), who are charged with taking creatures out of the storm of atoms.

The sincere one (mukhlis) is the secret of the souls and their elixir, illuminating souls and turning them to gold, casting upon them the good color of Allah (Sibghata-llah wa-man ahsanu mina-llahi sibghah).
The sciences of the da'wah, flowing from the hudud and the Imam's gaze, transform the believer's sensual animal soul into a speaking angelic soul (nafs natiqah malakiyyah).

The recipient of these truths is bound by a confirmed, strict covenant ('ahd) of Allah, the same covenant taken from the close angels, the sent prophets, the guiding Imams, and their rightly-guided hudud.
Allah took a covenant and oath of allegiance (bay'at) from the prophets in the Quran, first taking the Messenger's name, then Adam, Nuh, Ibrahim, Musa, and 'Isa.

The recipient is forbidden to copy or write down the discourse — not a single letter, neither less nor more — to inform anyone except the permitted, and must return the manuscript after finishing reading it.

The Unseen of the Unseen (ghayb al-ghuyub) cannot be comprehended by the mind, encompassed by thought, named, or attributed; the only valid confession is that for all the worlds there is an Originator whom intellects are powerless to comprehend.
Tawhid is the gnosis (ma'rifat) of the higher and lower hudud, not the gnosis of the Exalted Originator, whose gnosis is impossible.
Sayyidna Ja'far bin Sulayman taught that tawhid is not for the Worshipped One but is the gnosis of the hudud (at-tawhid laysa li'l-ma'bud wa-lakin at-tawhid ma'rifat al-hudud).
Without ma'rifat (gnosis of the hudud), one falls into heresy and disbelief (ma'rifat na kuni, zindiqi).
The rank of Sani (the Second) fell from Munba'ith because, though he confessed the Originator and had gnosis of 'Aql al-Awwal, he lacked the gnosis of Munba'ith al-Awwal and claimed to be his equal.
Tawhid requires confessing that every hadd is unique in his rank, with no partner sharing it (kullu haddin minhum wahidun fi rutbatihi).

In the kalima La ilaha illa-llah, among the spiritual intellects only 'Aql al-Awwal is worthy of the name 'Allah'; all others stand at the rank of ilah — just as in our age the higher and lower hudud are at the rank of ilah and only the Imam of the time is at the rank of Allah.

The kalima La ilaha illa huwa is higher than La ilaha illa-llah; it was 'Aql al-Awwal's confession of the Mubdi' (shahida-llahu annahu la ilaha illa huwa), using huwa for the Transcendent Ipseity (al-huwiyyat al-muta'aliyah), whereas the Prophet propagated La ilaha illa-llah.
The numerical (jumal) value of La ilaha illa huwa is 110, as in Surah al-Muzzammil's rabbu'l-mashriqi wa'l-maghribi la ilaha illa huwa fa-ttakhidhhu wakila.

In rabbu'l-mashriqi wa'l-maghribi, the east is Hasan (from whom the Imams rose) and the west is Abu'l-Qasim; all are organized in the being of Ali, and fa-ttakhidhhu wakila commands the Messenger to take Ali as his wasi.
rabbu'l-mashriqayni wa'l-maghribayni (Lord of the two easts and wests) signifies the Imams emerging from Mawlana Ali and ending with him.
Amir al-Mu'minin, in the book Saluni qabla an tafqiduni, exoterically explained the three Quranic forms (one east/west, two, and many) by the sun's rising and setting points across the year.
Tajrid (abstraction) is the stripping of divinity — the power to bring from non-existence to existence — from all originated and created things, and affirming it for their Originator.
Tanzih (transcendence) is the negation of all attributes from the Unseen of the Unseen, confessing that all nobility and majesty, and the divine names, fall upon the First Intellect ('Aql al-Awwal).
Tawhid, tajrid, and tanzih together constitute the essence of what has come from the masters regarding the doctrine of divine unity.
The Unseen of the Unseen originated the world of origination ('alam al-ibda') in a single instant, without time or space — time and space being later creations of the 'Ashir.
The Originator created innumerable luminous forms equal in the first perfection and first existence — life, power, and knowledge — by the requirement of His justice, with no one superior to another.
The intellects themselves ARE the spiritual world ('alam ruhani) and the World of Origination — luminous spirits with no density, no body, contained by no space, and needing no time.

Proof of the intellects' freedom from space and time: our own souls, a tiny part of that world, traverse the distance of east and west and conceive distant heavens and earth in less than the blink of an eye — so how much more for the complete, body-free intellects.

Human intellects are powerless to comprehend the least attribute of the forms of the World of Origination, so they cannot reach a way to comprehend their Originator, who is transcendently higher than all that.

The Indian and non-Arab (Ajami) du'at such as Ali bin Sulayman and Hasan Khan wrote with great clarity, whereas the Arab du'at, despite their high status, made matters obscure; Hasan Khan's 70 haqa'iq books require no dictionary.
To express something easily is harder than to express it obscurely; Sayyidna Hamiduddin al-Kirmani, da'i of the two Iraqs and a bab al-abwab, wrote Rahat al-'Aql clearly yet with deep subtleties.
Excessive grammar is unnecessary for reading the da'wah books; the maxim holds that until a person learns to read without understanding, he can never learn to read Arabic.
Every da'i commanded the people of his island that each marry a female formed in a cave other than his own; the woman formed from a man's own leftover water is like his sister and unlawful to marry.
This marriage rule is declared the pure and exalted path of truth (tariq al-haqq al-tahira al-munazzah).
Guidance belongs to Allah alone (wa ma kunna li-nahtadiya lawla an hadana Allah); Allah told even the Prophet, the greatest guide, that he cannot guide anyone.

The word 'huda' has the numerical value 19 (ha 5, dal 4, ya 10), and the names of the Ahl al-Bayt (Muhammad 4, Ali 3, Fatima 5, Hasan 3, Husayn 4) also total 19, corresponding to the 19 letters of Bismillah al-Rahman al-Rahim.
The blessing of the Quran comes from its beginning with Bismillah; therefore the Prophet instructed beginning every act with Bismillah so it will be blessed.
Iyyaka na'budu wa iyyaka nasta'in is a non-repeated phrase occurring only once in the Quran; non-repeated phrases hold greater virtue than repeated ones, and its letters total 19.
Among the muqatta'at, the non-repeated ones (Ya-Sin, Kaf-Ha-Ya-'Ayn-Sad, each once) hold virtue over the repeated ones (Alif-Lam-Mim many times, Ha-Mim seven times).
The verse ihdina's-sirat al-mustaqim is recited 51 times daily, and its letters total 19.
The straight path (sirat al-mustaqim) is the path of those upon whom Allah bestowed favor: the prophets, the truthful, the martyrs, and the righteous (alladhina an'amta 'alayhim).

Birth directly from the earth (clods) occurred only once, in a single first instance at the beginning of the cycle; thereafter procreation between men and women continued until now, and clod-birth will recur at the beginning of the next cycle.
From a single clod only one man and one woman were born — the woman from the man's leftover water and thus his sister — never many individuals.
On Sarandib (Ceylon) 28 clods were formed, and the most excellent among them was that of the juz'i ibda'iya (creative part).
The virtuous person (juz'i ibda'iya) brought forth and appointed his noble son to succeed him in his station, choosing him from his hudud and the people of his mission.
The author states he explained the reality of the beginning explicitly, without symbol or indication (musarrihan fi ghayri ramzin wa-la ishara).
Amir al-Mu'minin taught that a believer should know four things — where he came from, where he will go, how he came, and how he will go — which together constitute the subjects of mabda' and ma'ad.
When the respondent (mustajib) accepts at the hands of a hadd with pure intention toward his hadd and his Sahib al-Zaman, a point of light (nuqta min nur) connects with and neighbors his soul.
Muslim children in believers' houses are only potential believers; they become actual believers at the moment they take the 'ahd-i sharif (noble covenant).

The point of light neighbors the sensual soul without merging with it until death, illuminating and making it radiant; whatever the sensual soul accepts becomes part of the natiqa soul, and what it rejects remains sensual.
Only a small part of the point of light is received per cycle — a portion of the repentance one made in the spiritual world — because the soul cannot bear it in its entirety.

The point of light reaches the believer not directly but through the mediation of his high-ranking hadd; its origin is the substance and flowing support (maddah wa ta'id) from the Exalted Originator (Mubdi' Ta'ala).

The substance and support descends in a chain: from the Mubdi' to the First Preceding Intellect, then to all originating intellects, then to the Tenth, then to every noble station (Natiq, Wasi, or Imam) of the time, then to his higher hudud and downward to the respondent, each receiving according to his worthiness.
Those who take the 'ahd-i sharif do so with differing intentions and receive their portion accordingly.

As the respondent increases in good deeds, establishing the works of shari'ah (the seven pillars), constancy, benefiting from celestial sciences, sincere loyalty (muwalat) to the mawali, and acknowledging each hadd's virtue, his point of light grows, illuminates, and is purified and polished.
All righteous deeds are for the progress of one's own soul, and evil deeds are against it (man 'amila salihan fa-li-nafsihi wa man asa'a fa-'alayha).

The lowest illumination a believer receives is the point of light's illumination upon his sensual soul and body; the natiqa soul is so secretive it does not even inform its neighboring sensual soul (the conscience).

At a believer's last breath his place in paradise is shown to him, causing joy that spreads light on his face; Sayyidna Muhammad bin Fawad al-Qusu (Ghadanfar) carried this radiance his whole life for his services in saving the Da'wah-i Hadiya, and the du'at descend from his lineage until Qiyamah except for four.
Sayyidna Ali bin Sulayman foretold, before the chain of du'at was established, that the du'at would come from the lineage of Sayyidna Muhammad bin Fawad until Qiyamah.

Numerous miracles (mojizaat) are reported of Sayyidna Ali bin Sulayman — the multiplication of food invoking 'Ya Sayyidna Sulayman aghithni', a lost rupee returning upon his head, 500 garments arriving after he gave one away, and his prediction of a man's death by Wednesday — manifesting the blessings of the awliya' Allah's word.

Sayyidna Ali bin Sulayman authored Shu'a' al-Anwar (said to be in daqa'iq rather than haqa'iq) and Anwar al-Shashaniya, and served as da'i for about 35-38 years after the death of Sayyidna Ja'far in 1150.

The luminous form (surah) of the deceased mustajib transfers with each hadd to the one higher than him until it reaches the Bab al-Maqam, the Bab of the Imam of the Time and the greatest servant of the da'wah.

The collection of all luminous forms (suwar) happens at the Bab, not the Imam — analogous to the falak al-buruj gathering all stars while the encompassing falak al-muhit remains empty (bari'); no surah goes to the Imam.
Durud and salam are sent upon the Bab (the fatihu al-kitab) just as upon the Imam.
The luminous forms from all twelve islands (jaza'ir) of the earth gather at the Bab until a luminous structure (haykal nurani) in human form, entirely light, is assembled.

If the haykal nurani appeared to mortals it would dazzle and blind their sight, as no one can look at the sun; it is a spiritual, holy, pre-eternal (azali) light, far greater than the sun's physical light.
The haykal enters the son (farzand) of the Imam and, progressing, will one day become an intellect ('aql).
The Imam does not bestow imamat until the haykal's formation is complete and the ripe suwar gather; very sinful believers who did not repent are held back to be absorbed by the next Imam.
The Bab al-Abwab must also transfer physically (die); for example Mawlatuna Khadijah bint Khuwaylid, the Bab al-Abwab of Fatima, transferred when Mawlana Abu Talib died (three days after).

Each luminous form settles in the haykal according to what it earned in the world — in the position of the heart, brain, eye, ear, hand, foot, hair, nail, or sole — each according to its deed, with no injustice done.

The Bab is so named because the haykal with him is a collection of intellects; since the intellect ('aql) is the essence (lubb) of a life's surah, the Bab is the gatherer of all essences (jami' al-albab).
This haykal is named the Imamah; when the Imam meets the Imamah, the Imam's son goes from potentiality (bil-quwwah) to actuality (bil-fi'l), and then the Imam passes away.
When a believer's soul separates from his body, traces of the vegetative soul (nafs namiyyah) remain as innate heat, also called the winds (riyah).

Of the three souls (namiyyah, hissiyyah, natiqah), the riyah exit fully over three days; those leaving before burial are superior and form the Imam's higher hudud, while those leaving after burial are lower, given the moon's light, and form the Imam's body after purification.

The riyah are purified at the moon, Jupiter, and the sun over 360 years going, 360 returning, and 280 to moderate their temperament — a thousand years total — after which raj'at (return) occurs for all: believer, kafir, munafiq, and Muslim alike.

A believer's three souls unite to form the luminous surah sharif, whereas a kafir, mushrik, or murtadd has no natiqah formed — only namiyyah and hissiyyah manifest in his body, his basest form, and he feels the divine punishment after death.
All souls return after a thousand years; those who fell to the lower realms (darkat) return from there, the da'wah is presented to them, and if they persist they face punishment.
The enemies (azdad) are resurrected in physical form when the Qa'im comes and see the Qa'im as the Imam of their own time — Yazid sees Imam Husayn, Mu'awiyah sees Ali — before the Imam punishes them.
Non-believers are raised with their own imams of misguidance (a'immah al-dalalah, mentioned in the Quran) in the time of the Qa'im.

The windy souls (riyah) fully exit on the third day, which is why Sadaq Allah is recited; good deeds, charity, and prayers within those three days benefit the deceased's body, while later Fatiha gatherings do not.

The purified soul ascends as a subtle vapor to the moon (received by its rays), then via Mercury and Venus to the sun, then to Jupiter; the sun and Jupiter purify the riyah until the suwar at the Bab are complete.

When the Director (Mudabbir) permits the appearance of the Imamic personage, the sun returns the purified windy souls to the moon via Venus and Mercury, and the moon's rays send them to pure water or a noble fruit, descending in a dew drop that only the Imam can attain.
The Prophet said an apple came from Allah, of which he and Khadija each ate half, after which Fatima al-Zahra was born — the same process of the Imamic substance descending in a noble fruit.
The Mudabbir Ta'ala repeatedly mentioned is the 'Ashir, though Hazrat 'Abdullah Sahib held it means the Juz'-i Idayi (Creative Part) of this cycle.

The Imam and his noble, pure wife eat the prepared fruit and unite in marriage, whereupon it becomes a nutfah (sperm-drop) for the Imamic personage, the haykal drawing sustenance from the remaining nourishment.
The mothers of the Imams (Ummahat al-A'immah) are purified (batul) from menstrual blood; though the Imam has several wives, the one from whom his son is born is the batul.

Per Mawla Shaykh Husayn (confirmed by Sayyidna Ali bin Husayn al-Mukarrami), a woman becomes one of the Ummahat al-A'immah as reward for great services rendered as a mansub or da'i in a previous existence, though she returns in female form.
The verse innama yuridu Allahu li-yudhhiba 'ankum al-rijs Ahl al-Bayt wa yutahhirakum tathira praises the Ahl al-Bayt and the Ummahat al-A'immah as far removed from impurity and menstrual blood.
The Imam's son receives nourishment through a nine-month gestation, digesting like an ordinary child, then is born with a noble, camphor-like (kafuri) body made of ru'yah.
The completion of the Bab al-Abwab's surat and the birth of the Imam's son run exactly in parallel (sawa'an bi sawa'an); the Imamah cannot be given until the body's formation is complete.
The Bab passes away and his noble rational soul (nafs natiqah), carrier of all the suwar, connects with the Imam's son; this occurs in a minimum of forty days and a maximum of four years.

As an exception, Mawlana 'Abd al-Muttalib received the haykal from his father Hashim during his mother Salma's pregnancy, before birth, because his station is great as the grandfather of the 'Ayn and the Mim (Ali and Muhammad).

The luminous haykal radiates upon the ghilaf (covering, the Imam's body or nasut); the haykal is the Imamah and the camphor body is the Imam, so the Imam is lower (adna) and the Imamah higher (bar-tar), and their union turns the son from potentiality to actuality.
The Imam's body is called the ghilaf, the shibh kafuri (camphor-like form), and the nasut, while the luminous haykal (collection of suwar) is called the Lahut.

Anwar and asrar are distinct: asrar means the ri'yah and anwar means the suwar; per Sayyidna Ali bin Hiba al-Makrami in Kunuz al-Hikmah, the secrets gathered from the first Da'i Sayyidna Dhu'ayb bin Musa to Sayyidna Sulayman bin Hasan.
There are multiple types of nasut — natural (tabi'i), shadow (dhilli), and special (khas) — and the lawa'ih and lahut vary correspondingly, each nasut being a covering opposite its lahut.

The sensory soul (nafs hissiyah) of the Imam's son carries the luminous haykal and is higher than the rational soul (natiqah) of the Bab, having the power to gather all the suwar — du'at, hujjatayn, mu'minin, ma'dhunin, hudud, and the Bab himself.
The sensory soul of Amir al-Mu'minin was superior to all the lawa'ih of the pure Imams from Mawlana Hunayd to Abu'l-Qasim, except for the three sufara'.

When the father designates (nass) his son for the people of his time, the flowing substance (maddah sariyah) connects to the son through the father and everyone above him up to the First Intellect, an unbroken connection from the corporeal world to the spiritual world.
Through this designation the substance becomes a veil (hijab) and gate (bab) for the son, because the Imam directs his gaze specifically toward him from among the hudud of the world of religion.

The gaze descends in hierarchy: Munba'ith al-Awwal gazed to his Bab, each lower intellect to its veil, and every creative intellect to a hadd of the world of religion, so the substance of guidance flows from top to bottom across the ages.

The designated Imam receives the substance from the hudud until he brings forth his own successor; a Da'i munfarid's very first thought is who his successor will be (awwal al-fikr wa akhir al-'amal — the first thought and the last action).
Ranks are not attained without tests; the da'wah's history is full of trials, and Amir al-Mu'minin declared that Allah tested him fourteen times — seven by the Messenger and seven by Allah.
The Imam brings forth a second son to succeed him in his station, exactly as his own father did before him (sawa'an bi sawa'an, with no difference).

The first Imam, having designated his successor, ascends into the horizon of the Tenth ('ufuq al-'ashir / barzakh-i 'ashiriyyah) and becomes governor of the world (mudabbir al-'alam), while the 'Ashir ascends to a higher rank.

These are partial successorships (juzwi khilafat), not total (kulli); the total successorship of the 'Ashir occurs in one mawr, after which the 'Ashir becomes the Ninth Intellect and progresses upward toward the Munba'ith al-Awwal.

Ten mawrs complete the gathering of the whole realm into intellects congregating at the Munba'ith al-Awwal, leaving only two states: the sphere of the First Intellect (sphere of unity, containing no intellect) and the sphere of the Munba'ith al-Awwal (containing all intellects) — like the empty falak muhit versus the star-filled falak buruj.

When a successor is present, the Da'i appoints no one himself; all rulings flow through the successor (la yunazzilu al-da'i ayya shakhs fi wujud khalifatihi) — illustrated by the nass chains of Ali bin Mawsin al-Shibam, Ghulam Husayn, and Ali bin Sulayman.
Whether a da'i was ghayr-munfarid is known only after his passing; before that he holds the rank of khalifah al-da'i (successor of the Da'i).

The nass chain ran: Ali bin Sulayman to Ibrahim bin Muhammad al-Fahd, whose son Isma'il died in his time, so he designated his nephew Muhammad bin Isma'il, who designated Hasan Khan bin 'Abd al-Malik (who died), then Hibatullah.

Sayyidna Ali bin Hibatullah al-Makrami was the best surah in the congregation of Sayyidna Isma'il bin Hiba, who always sought his intercession in his books; al-Kawakib al-Durriyah was authored in his father's lifetime.

Sayyidna Isma'il bin Hibatullah was eighth in his father's ranking yet designated successor; Hibatullah wrote the tartib (ranking) of his father's hudud, in which the master of the two islands India and Sindh, Sayyidi al-Mansur Karamullah, was the twenty-eighth.

The ascension of the intellects' ranks continues until the third of them reaches the first of the seven intellects in the sphere of the Munba'ith al-Awwal, called hadirat al-quds, which is the final end of the cycles (adwar) and eras (akwar).
No one has access to the rank of the Sabiq al-Awwal (the First Intellect), because it is the rank of unity (rutbat al-wahdah).

When the possessor of the creative body (jussah ibda'iyyah) ascends to the rank of the Tenth after bringing forth his son, he ascends to the horizon of his father, and every Imam after him ascends to him, all remaining in the horizon of the 'Ashir until the Qa'im rises.

The departed pure Imams connect at their Bab, and the Qa'im's Bab al-Abwab is Mawlana Ali, in whom the luminous haykals gathered from Mawlana Hunayd to Abu'l-Qasim (except the three sufara'), across seven cycles of unveiling and seven of concealment.

The sensory soul of Amir al-Mu'minin is the accumulator of the haykals of the Imams of every cycle, uniquely gathering both the previous AND the future Imams (al-awwal wa'l-akhir), unlike any other Imam who gathers only those before him.

A great temple (haykal 'azim) forms for the Bab al-Abwab Ali, every Imam being a limb of it, so that at the Qa'im's hands will be the reckoning (hisab) and reward (thawab) that all previous Imams deferred to him.

The Qa'im brings forth a son from his da'wah and ascends with all the maqamat, which become a single form; the Qa'im's son will be the first Imam of the dawr al-kashf (the second cycle), and is mustaqarr, not mustawda'.
The Qa'im succeeds with the rank of qiyamah; his son is his successor only in the Imamah, not in the rank of qiyamah, for the last Imam of the concealed cycle becomes the next Qa'im.
The coming Qa'im was the successor of the previous cycle's Qa'im, all gathered with Mawlana Ali, so that Ali became the wasi (executor) of the Qa'im.
Sayyidna Isma'il bin Hibatullah states that the Qa'im will have only one son, not two like Mawlana Ali's Hasan and Husayn, and from him the Imamah will continue.

In the dawr al-sitr the Imamah continued not from Hasan but from Husayn; Hasan performed no nass on his son Qasim because Husayn was an infallible born one (mawlud ma'sum) already designated by the Prophet.
Designation (nass wa tawqif) is obligatory; the Prophet performed nass on Hasan and Husayn, and Mawlana Ali confirmed the Prophet's will at the end of his life (akkada wasiyyat Rasulillah).
Hasan is subsumed within Husayn (al-Hasanu fi al-Husayn) — Hasan is present within Husayn, even within the letters of his name.
Upon the Qa'im's hands will be the reckoning (hisab), the reward (sawab), and the punishment (iqab) — the major decisions of the resurrection.
The Qa'im's veil (hijab/occultation) will not last more than three days because his are the highest riyahat, which cannot remain longer in the world; then he appoints his son.
The Qa'im has a new glory each day (kullu yawmin huwa fi sha'n), being the essence of all cycles (adwar) and spheres (akwar), since all the stations of the Pure Imams consolidate in him.
The Qa'im's likeness is like an intellect of the World of Origination, and he succeeds the Tenth in his rank — a partial successorship (khilafat juzwi), not total.

The Qa'im manages the world through substance (maddah) and support (ta'id) in a partial management, and the stations transfer to his horizon, one imam after another, until the second Qa'im of the resurrection rises.

In the dawr al-kashf a Qa'im rises every thousand years, so 47,000 years yield 47,000 Qa'ims; the seventh gathers the previous six (7, 14, 21, 28, 35, 42), and the 47,000-year Qa'im is the true Qa'im of the dawr al-kashf of most magnificent glory.
Mawlana Hunaid gathers the remaining 3,000 years of the dawr al-fatrat, as Sayyidna Ali bin Sulayman mentioned that the Qa'im of the dawr al-kashf gathered 47,000 years (not 50,000).
Known history extends only from Adam; what came before was deliberately erased from human minds by the da'wah's will, and science describes earlier artifacts only partially (juzwi), not completely.

This esoteric knowledge came through ta'id and is all implicitly present in the Quran (kashf, sitr, adwar, akwar are not explicit but are contained there); per Ghulam Husayn Sahib, the Quran is the true source and repository, and the Dawoodi sciences agree up to Sayyidna Burhanuddin.

The total dawr al-kashf spans 50,000 years (47,000 pure kashf plus 3,000 fatrat); at its end evil increases and good decreases, so it is resolved that the haqa'iq be cut off and concealed after having been openly manifest, recited on the minbar and in gatherings.
After concealment, the haqa'iq reach only the one who seeks them from their proper doors (abwab) through covenants ('uhud) and strict pledges (mawathiq).

The dawr al-sitr begins with Adam, the first of the nuqata'; Nuh, who came after, was the first of the Ulul-'Azm and brought a new shari'ah, whereas Adam is a nuqata' but not Ulul-'Azm (lam najid lahu 'azma).
Each subsequent natiq — Ibrahim, Musa, 'Isa, and Muhammad — brought a new shari'ah abrogating that of his predecessor.

The cycles of the prophets correspond to stages of embryonic creation relative to the awaited Qa'im: Adam's cycle is the shadow (zill), Nuh's the drop (nutfah), Ibrahim's the clot ('alaqah), Musa's the lump (mudghah), 'Isa's the bones ('izam), and Muhammad's the flesh (lahm) — hence the Prophet's love of meat.

Sayyidna Ali bin Sulayman in Jinan al-Jinan demonstrated that the three 'ulama of the era (Sulayman bin Hasan, Muhammad bin Fahd, Ja'far bin Sulayman) are the essence of the du'at, the letters of their names coinciding with those of the hudud of every cycle from Adam onward.

Anecdote: the narrator's letter-matching of the hudud of Sayyidna Husayn bin Hasan was corrected by Sayyidna, who knew which figures truly were among his hudud and which were not (e.g. Abdullah was a mansub, Muhsin Shayba was not), illustrating that a believer sees with the light of Allah.
Every maqam — natiq, wasi, or imam — from Adam to the last Imam of Muhammad's cycle, upon transferring, settles in the horizon of the Tenth and manages the world of nature, until Abu al-Qaim is born.
The last Imam of Muhammad's cycle is the Qa'im al-qiyamah; all who transferred from Adam to him connect with him, his noble soul becoming their carrier, and all become a single luminous form.
The Qa'im appears with his hujjah preceding him in the da'wah; this hujjah is the Mahdi of the End of Time, who comes before the Qa'im.

It is among the possibilities that the Qa'im (if the present Imam is Abu al-Qaim) has already been born; his birth from the Ka'ba is not established (unlike Mawla Ali's), and he is muhayyir al-rutbah (one who confounds the ranks).

Sayyidna Idris bin Hasan in Subur al-Sabi' states that when the Qa'im rises his age will be 37 — the number of times 'La ilaha illa Allah' occurs in the Quran (37 times across 36 verses in five different forms).

La ilaha illa Anta is the only non-repeated form, occurring once in the Quran in the supplication of the prophet Yunus (la ilaha illa anta inni kuntu min az-zalimin), to which Allah responded instantly (fa-istajabna lahu), and thus the believers too are saved.

Allah gives the hujjah possession of the entire earth and compels obedience: he loses the first battle (the Romans win), wins the second, and the seven continents come under his control; when he declares himself a servant of the Qa'im the people turn away, and then the great gathering (hashr) occurs.

The hujjah proclaims in all horizons that whoever chooses a religion may adhere to it and be safe, so everyone manifests his belief; with the appearance of falsehood (batil), the matter becomes severe for the people of truth.
Sayyidna Husayn (a sutrah of the qiyamah) taught that the Qa'im appears with knowledge and the sword both, and indicated that the entire reality of the qiyamah is contained within Surah al-Fatiha.

Surah al-Fatiha has seven verses and 25 words, corresponding to the 25 prophets named in the Quran and indicating the Imam's system: 12 daytime hudud (in the islands), 12 nighttime hudud (in his presence), and the Imam himself as the 25th.

Sayyidna Hasan bin Hamid bin Malik holds that Surah al-Fatiha encodes the number of Imams via 'hamd' (ha 8 + mim 40 + dal 4 = 52): 49 Imams from Hasan to Abu al-Qaim plus the Prophet, Ali, and Fatima, after which the qiyamah occurs.

The qaim al-qiyamah appears suddenly (baghtatan); all creation from all horizons gathers, and the first and the last are assembled at the appointed time (innal-awwalina wal-akhirina la-majmu'una ila miqati yawmin ma'lum) — the known day being the Qa'im and the miqat their place of meeting with him.

Before the Qa'im, every imam, hadd, believer, and their opposites (azdad) take form; he makes them aware of their deeds and commands the believers to slaughter all the azdad as at Mina, after which a fire descends from the sky to burn them before they descend to the greater punishment of Sijjin/Saqar in the lowest earth.

Punishment is of three types: the nearer ('adhab adna, the rah khunnar of seven levels), the intermediate ('adhab awsat, ice within the poles and mountains), and the greater ('adhab akbar, Saqar — the most severe, where the azdad of the da'wah are kept for one great cycle, punished by the moon's light by day and the sun's by night, killed and revived a thousand times nightly, neither dying nor living).

The 'known day' (yawm ma'lum) gathering is for those in the da'wah; the opposites of Adam, Nuh, and the rest come in human form and are punished through the believers by the Qa'im, while many who are not opposites are spared.

After the judgment the Qa'im appoints his son caliph, ascends with all the maqamat under his charge, becomes caliph of the Tenth, and proceeds with his son for the 50,000 years of the dawr al-kashf, which alternates between unveiling (kashf) and concealment (sitr).

There are three cycles: the pure dawr al-kashf (founded upon haqa'iq), the dawr al-fatrat (founded upon ta'wil, 3,000 years of sluggishness), and the dawr al-sitr (founded upon shari'ah, 7,000 years); the fatrat, though at the end of the kashf, is counted within the dawr al-sitr.
Mawlana Ali said that every 10,000 years a form appears and that form is him, combining the 3,000 years of fatrat and the 7,000 years of sitr.

Every maqam — prophet, wasi, or imam — is connected to the substance from the First Intellect perpetually, without interruption for even the blink of an eye, as the Quran says la ta'khudhuhu sinatun wa la nawm (neither slumber nor sleep overtakes Him), meaning neither complete nor partial inattention.
key_terms: la takhudhuhu sinatun wa la nawm

teaching: Every station (maqam) — whether of a prophet, a wasi, or an Imam — is connected by the maddah (substance) that flows from the First Intellect.
The maddah is always issued continuously from the First Intellect and never ceases.
The First Intellect is named 'al-Hayy al-Qayyum' (the Ever-Living, the Self-Sustaining) in the Quran; this is its attribute.
The Greatest Name of Allah (Ism al-A'zam) is present within 'al-Hayy al-Qayyum', as it is within 'Ya Dhal-Jalali wal-Ikram'.
The tasbih (glorification) assigned to Sunday is 'al-Hayy al-Qayyum'.
The Dua al-Hayat is said to contain the Ism al-A'zam (though not pinpointed); it was revealed separately from Allah, not in the manner of the Quran.
The Dua al-Hayat is a du'a of Maulana 'Ali, who valued it so highly that he kept it in his turban.

The Ism al-A'zam refers to the First Intellect, not to the mubda' ta'ala (Transcendent Originator), who is beyond all names, indications, and qualities; all dealings occur through the First Intellect.

'al-Hayy al-Qayyum' means the First Intellect both lives by the maddah received from the mubda' ta'ala and gives life by passing it to lower intellects according to their capacity to receive (istiqhaq), never giving all of what it receives.
The intellects after the First Intellect differ in precedence (sabaqiyat) and acuity of vision (hiddat-e-nazar), but their understanding is the same.
The Originator created every intellect with the same first-level endowment of three powers — knowledge, life, and power; how each subsequently used them determined its rank.
The chain of maddah and ta'yid flows continuously from the First Intellect and is not cut off even for the blink of an eye (la yanqati'u turfata 'ayn).

When a prophet, wasi, or Imam manifests power, miracles, and actions that bewilder the intellects of creatures, that action is attributed to the higher one who looks upon him — the muhtajib (veiled one) and mumiddu (aider).
When a prophet, wasi, or Imam manifests weakness, pain, illness, or human states, that is attributed to the ghilaf (covering) / hijab / nasut (human form), not to the essential self.
The nasut is extracted from the world of nature (alam al-tabi'ah), formed from the airy souls (nufus rihiyyah), and obtained through physical birth (wiladat jismaniyyah).
Ghulu (raising an Imam above his station) and qulu/qassar (diminishing him below his station) are both impermissible.
When some elevated Maulana 'Ali to divinity, he warned them, and when they refused to listen he ordered them burned; later du'at like Mughira did the same regarding Ja'far al-Sadiq.
One must not believe that any prophet, wasi, or Imam is an originating god (ilah mubdi') or lord; they merely nurture lower ranks with the wisdom (hikmah) by which they are aided from above.

All stations and hudud negate divinity and lordship from themselves, affirming that the power to originate from nothing belongs only to the mubda' ta'ala, Originator of all (Mubdi' al-kull) and their Creator.
Quran: 'And whoever of them says, I am a god besides Him — that one We recompense with Hell; thus do We recompense the wrongdoers.'
Nimrod's punishment is more severe than Yazid's because Nimrod claimed divinity for himself while Yazid did not.
The word jaza' (recompense) carries two senses — punishment and reward.

Many people, seeing the dazzling miracles and astounding deeds manifested at 'Ali's hands, committed ghulu and claimed he was a god who creates and provides, neither born nor begetting and without equal — which Allah cursed as misguidance (dalal) and disbelief (kufr).

The correct obligatory belief is that the Prophet Muhammad is the most excellent of the intellects of the world of nature (afdalu 'uqul al-'alam al-tabi'ah) and the noblest of the world of the hudud of religion.
The 'intellects of the world of nature' are those presently in potentiality (bil-quwwah) — the veils — who will one day become actual intellects.
The miracles 'Ali manifested were from the support (ta'yid) of the First Intellect, and reached him only through the mediation of the Prophet.
The Prophet remains the mediator (wasita) for everything always, even after his passing.

Jibra'il conveyed his salam to 'Ali and declared the Prophet 'sayyid al-anbiya wal-mursalin wa khatam al-nabiyyin' and 'Ali 'Amir al-Mu'minin'; thus the title Amir al-Mu'minin came to 'Ali from Allah through Jibra'il.
Every Imam of the time is Amir al-Mu'minin, but when 'Amir al-Mu'minin' is said without a name it denotes 'Ali ibn Abi Talib.
The Prophet is 'Ali's hadd, teacher, nurturer, and the one who raised him to his rank; he made 'Ali his successor (caliph) in his community, and 'Ali is his hujjat in his lifetime.
The Prophet's rank in the physical world corresponds to the First Intellect (al-'aql al-awwal al-sabiq), and 'Ali's rank in religion corresponds to the first emanation (munba'ath al-awwal).
The Prophet is like the male (dhakar) and the sky (sama'); 'Ali is like the female who accepts from him (untha qabilah) and the earth (ard) that absorbs the pure water descending from the sky.
Quran 'wa ta'iyaha udhunun wa'iyah' (that a retaining ear might retain it) refers to 'Ali, who said 'that ear is me' (tilka al-udhun ana) and is called 'udhun khayr' (an ear of goodness).

After the Prophet's death 'Umar regretted unasked questions; 'Ali answered them — e.g. that dreams during the sensory soul's ascent through the heavens are true and those on its return are false — having remembered what 'Umar had forgotten.

Nothing is received directly from the First Intellect; in the present life the Prophet is the last and closest intermediary, while 'Ali's sermon 'ana al-awwal, ana al-akhir' relates to the 'ayn level.
'Ali said the Messenger taught him a thousand chapters from his treasured hidden knowledge, and from each chapter a thousand more opened ('allamani Rasulullah min makhnun 'ilmihi alfa bab).

At 'Ali's birth (from Fatima bint Asad in the Kaaba) he fixed his first gaze on the Prophet, who said 'khassastani bin-nazr wa khassastuka bil-'ilm' and 'Ana madinat al-'ilm wa 'Ali babuha', though his mother had named him Haidar.
key_terms: Ana madinat al-ilm wa Ali babuha

teaching: When the Prophet passed, 'Ali stood in the world of religion at the station of the First Intellect, and his hujjat (Bibi Fatima Zahra) at the station of the first emanation (munba'ath al-awwal).
Fatima Zahra is the successor (khalifa) of the Prophet — her footsteps fall where his fall — and the greatest hujjat of her husband: 'hujjatu ba'liha wa khalifatu abiha'.

It is obligatory to believe that the Prophet and 'Ali are in a single station and single rank (manzilah wahidah, martabah wahidah) with no superiority of one over the other, differing only in precedence (sabaqiyat).
The Prophet illustrated his equality with 'Ali by joining the index and middle fingers ('ana wa anta ya 'Ali ka-hatayn'), where one finger precedes — indicating Abu Talib always preceded the Prophet.
key_terms: ana wa anta ya Ali ka-hatayn

teaching: Whoever raises one of the Prophet/'Ali pair and lowers the other commits ghulu and falls short (qassara); the curse of Allah is upon anyone who holds the contrary belief.
Having explained the reality of the beginning (ibtida') and the praiseworthy return of the believers, the text turns to the unpraiseworthy return — 'wa hadha haqiqatu al-ibtida' wa al-ma'ad'.
The author has unveiled these matters explicitly and plainly without symbol or indication; such speech is unveiled only by the great Du'at, who are 'our hudud', and a prayer is made for their reward.
Knowing the return of the opponents completes the believer's form and elevates his rank (li-taktamila suratuka), just as 'la ilaha illa Allah' requires knowing both its negation and affirmation.
Knowledge is of two kinds — knowing the awliya Allah and knowing the opponents who are other than them — and both are necessary.

One should strive in good deeds to join the noble company in the sacred enclosure (hadhirat al-quds) — Bab al-Abwab, where the forms of the twelve islands gather — in the vicinity of Rabb al-'alamin, who is the Imam of the Time.
The opponent of truth, through his hostility, acquires the deeds of the people of evil, which form a dark form (suratun zulmaniyyah) — the inverse of the believer's luminous form.
At death the opponent's dark form (his vile concept) is stripped away, terrifying and alienating him — this is the first of its punishments.
The dark form's origin is the darkness that fell upon him at the time of his sin in the world of beginning (alam al-ibtida'), when he did not heed the 'ashir and did not repent.

This darkness, the head and tail (ra's wa dhanab, i.e. Rahu and Ketu), acts as a magnet for the dark satanic forms because of the affinity (munasabah) between them — 'as the person is, so are his angels'.
Ra's wa dhanab (Rahu and Ketu) lie below the sphere of the moon; they are not a planetary sphere but conceptual, non-visible places that nonetheless exist, serving as a center for the vile forms.
The vile forms residing there produce the harmful sorrows of the world, troubling and perplexing the believers.

Those in the lowest ranks can ascend gradually from being musirr (insistent on sin), for qudrat wills that the insistent and wretched enter faith; this occurs across the cycles (adwar) and eras (aqwar).

Those who ascend are entrusted with very great services spanning entire cycles (adwar), gaining great luminosity and transparency, so that on their return in human form they reach very high stations; some current du'at were formerly musirrin and mustakbirin (arrogant).
There are three punishments: the lowest ('adhab al-adna), the middle ('adhab al-awsat), and the greatest ('adhab al-akbar).

The lowest punishment ('adhab al-adna) occurs in the physical world, descending through human (Zanj/Habshi), then bear and monkey, wild animals, birds, down to the mineral level, ending in tar where no da'wah is presented.

At each change of form the da'wah of the Imam of the Time is presented; acceptance (which is rare) leads to ascent and refusal to descent, until the tar punishment where no argument or da'wah is offered — a mercy of qudrat that ends there.

Volcanic lava represents souls being returned toward human form, released from the punishment of rock; the land becoming fertile signifies their ascent, and the minerals (namaz) that form, when eaten, carry them upward.

Lunar and solar eclipses are caused by the vile forms gaining mastery over and awareness of the Imam's hidden plans, whereupon their mischief against believers increases; hence one should be engaged in prayer and supplication during an eclipse.

At the death of the Prophet's son Ibrahim a solar eclipse occurred; the Prophet rejected the people's claim that it was connected to his son's death, declaring the eclipse a sign of Allah with no connection to it.

When the Prophet wished to enter Ibrahim's grave, Mawla al-Ka'inat ('Ali) descended instead; and Ibrahim was made a ransom for Imam Husayn, Jibril having offered the Prophet a choice of which to be tried.

The Prophet wept over his four-year-old son Ibrahim (son of Mariyah al-Qibtiyyah); challenged by the hypocrites, he declared his natural grief — without mourning rites or tearing clothes — permissible.
Hypocrites (munafiqun) arose only in Madinah; in Makkah there were only disbelievers and polytheists or Muslims.

A gathering of the young children of past prophets who died young assembled at Ibrahim's death and later passed to Bibi Fatima, who is therefore called 'khulasatu al-jawhar al-islami' (the essence of the Islamic jewel).
Those who died before the wilayah of 'Ali was proclaimed also passed to Bibi Fatima's gathering, in which the highest form is that of Mawlana Hamzah.

Among the opponents, those of few sins who answered a prophet's call, submitted, and served are ground (sahik) and then ascend through the praiseworthy isthmus (barzakh al-su'ud) in minerals, plants, and animals until they obtain human form, then respond and ascend.

Ascent occurs only by accepting the noble da'wah / the call of the Imam of the Time; prayer, Hajj, and zakat alone are of no avail (though they bring one nearer), and consciously accepting the noble da'wah is the noblest deed.
Children who died young — such as Ibrahim and Asghar bin Husayn — hold very high ranks, the ranks of great du'at, despite having had no consciousness of the da'wah.

In the opponent's return, his vile conception departs before his body; his body is buried after his soul has spread within it — a degradation, since it is reprehensible for the high soul to spread in the body.
Cremation produces the same state as burial but with greater punishment, because the cremated have hastened and inflicted upon themselves the punishment of fire.

From the opponent (disbeliever, polytheist, enemy) and from all animals only the airy soul (nafs hawaiyyah) — the vapor he inhaled — departs at death, whereas from the believer the spiritual souls (nufus rihiyyah) depart.

When the opponent's body is buried it rots and stinks and writhes in the dust, and each of the four humors returns to its element-mother: yellow bile to fire, blood to air, phlegm to water, black bile to dust — gradually; this is the first of his punishments.
All of this is preserved by the power of the Planner (qudrat al-mudabbir); the ascending parts gather as rain in another form, dissolve into the dust, and become plants that are eaten.

The impure forms shelter in wildernesses, wastelands, filthy places, sewers, streams, and ravines, appear in people's dreams, and incite acts of lewdness in enmity to the people of truth; they are the blameworthy jinn, the devils (shayatin), and rebellious 'afarit harmful to mankind.
The believer's first reward is that his luminous form appears with radiance upon his body at the time of his death.

Sayyidna Muhammad Burhanuddin in Al-Anwar al-Latifah explains that when a believer dies a comforting light appears, which is the gathered happiness he brought to his believing brethren in life, given the form of light.

The dark form departs from the deceased opponent's soul and roams the horizon seeking to ascend (impossible) and to re-enter the body for its bodily pleasures (impossible), then roams the air — what the common people call munaf — with a forty-day respite.
The term munaf denotes the screaming and wailing born of dread (wahshat), and is not the plural of munif (from anf, meaning high-nosed / honorable).

The vile conceptions descend (hulul) into an ignorant impure woman, a dirty boy, or the like, possess them, speak through their tongues, whisper, and command sin; sometimes they leave and sometimes they cling until death.

Possession requires a pre-existing inclination in the host, for 'al-khabithuna lil-khabithat wal-khabithat lil-khabithin' (evil is for evil); without inclination nothing can occur, and even the awliya Allah are not wholly free of such inclinations.

Children who do not purify after the washroom spread impurity, and devils lick the hands of children who sleep with food on them, causing their night crying; therefore children's hands and feet should be washed before sleep.
The du'a 'Allahumma khalaqtani' states that the devil runs unseen in our blood, whispering and urging evil; qudrat nonetheless preserves us through our prayers, good deeds, and intentions.
The Prophet's prayers are short and easy to memorize, and through them he conferred great graces and protections upon the ummah.

Jibril taught the Prophet the prayer 'Allahumma inni as'aluka al-'afw wa al-'afiyah wa al-mu'afah fi al-dunya wa al-akhirah, ya arham al-rahimin' for times of worry or sickness, which the Prophet reserved for the Muslim ummah rather than himself.

Sayyidna 'Ali bin Sulayman compiled short prayers taught by Sayyidna Muhammad bin Fahd, including the tasbih 'Amanun min Allah wa Rasulihi, ya sayyidi, ya karim', on whose realities nearly forty pages were written.

After a bad death the impure forms endure seven plunges of punishment (al-nahas), the first being cast in the form of a Zanj (Abyssinian human form); when such a one is eaten by a male and female, an evil offspring resembling his parents appears.
The opponent's soul spreads in his body (a regression), becomes dense with sins, then dies and dissolves to become a plant, and passes through forms of monkeys, langurs, and bears.
Incantations (ruqa), amulets (aza'im), and the recitation of the Quran drive these forms away in cases of seizure/epilepsy (sar'); they flee and turn away.

The forms shelter in dreadful filthy places, bathhouses, and places where wine is drunk, then ascend to the tail (dhanab) — the two knots (ughdatayn), a darkness called dhanab and ra's outside the celestial sphere — and are nourished as monkeys, dogs, and pigs and all blameworthy forms.

The forms become a killing-poison plant (bitter and destructive), descend lower, then enter the most blameworthy minerals — glass (zaj), sulfur (kibrit), iron (hadid), lead (usas), and brass — before passing into animals.

The opponent's return is by transformation (istihalah) and birth (wiladah), NOT by the soul transferring from a dead body into another; the doctrine of transmigration (tanasukh) is misguidance and ignorance whose believer is destroyed and cursed.

When the lesser punishment (seven stages) is completed near the rising of the Qa'im, the opponent is joined with fire, becomes a plant eaten by his kind, a human person is born, is gathered at the rising of the Qa'im, rebuked for his past deeds, slaughtered, burned by fire descending from the ether, and led to Sijjin (the rock, Sakhar) to abide in the greatest punishment.

The Great Cycle of the greatest punishment lasts 360,000 years (stated as three hundred thousand plus one hundred thousand plus sixty and one thousand), and is reckoned as 360,000 multiplied by 360,000.
There is no remorse during the greatest punishment; remorse exists only in the lesser punishment, at every cycle (karr) and plunge (ghark), for at the greatest the pen has dried (jaffa al-qalam).
The greatest punishment (Sakhar, one Great Cycle) is only for the great opposites (azdad al-kibar) who opposed and killed the awliya Allah, and for the essence of sins, the wicked, and the evil.
The general rabble (kafat al-hamaj al-ri'a' — ignorant followers of evil) do not reach the greatest punishment, by Allah's care, because every servant is recompensed only by the measure of his deed.

From the deceased rabble only the airy soul departs; he dissolves through the isthmuses to the lesser punishment per his deeds, returns by transformation and birth to human form, and is presented the da'wah — purified if he responds, returned to deserved punishment a second time if he refuses — because Allah is Just, does not oppress, and does not break His promise.
The entire purpose of the genesis of creation is its purification and salvation from sin; whoever is purified ascends, while whoever refuses and shows enmity to the hudud is inverted and falls.
The believer is exhorted to be eager for action, purification, and the lightening of sins, and not to be deceived by the transient world.
'Ali said 'takhaffafu talhaqu' (lighten yourselves and you will catch up), for 'the first of you await the arrival of the last of you' (fa-innama yantaziru bi-awwalikum qudum akhirikum).
This teaching is the secret of the celestial realm (sirr al-malakut), entrusted as a trust (amanah) to be protected and concealed from everyone except those named.

Some who ascend reach the rank of bab al-abwab after thousands of years of service; du'at, ma'adhib, and hudud al-da'wah who serve sincerely are recompensed with high ranks in their future cycles (karrat).

The mothers of the Imams (ummahat al-a'immah) are infallible (ma'sumah), batul (without menstrual blood), and pure; they attain this honor because 'service has preceded them' (qad sabaqathunna al-khidam) in the times of the Imams, as with Muhammad bin al-Walid or Muhammad bin Fawad.

In the next cycle (wahdah) the template is the same but succession (khilafat) is established; the higher veil ascends and becomes the muhtajib — so high it becomes a veil for other veils — and the purified excesses (fuzalat) ascend to become their veils (hijabat).

Salman al-Farsi was born a Parsi non-Muslim in Fars, hidden since childhood, came in search of truth, and reached Madinah around 2 Hijri (absent throughout the Makkan period); brought as a slave, the Prophet freed him via 300 date palms planted by him and 300 by the Muslims plus gold.
Salman recognized the Prophet by three signs: that he accepts a gift but does not eat charity, and that the seal of prophethood was on his back.
Because of Salman's great spiritual progress, 'Salman minna Ahl al-Bayt' (Salman is from us, the Ahl al-Bayt) was declared.

The Ahl al-Bayt do not eat zakat because zakat is filth (mayl) and they are pure; and in Quran 'khudh min amwalihim sadaqatan...', 'salli 'alayhim' means 'pray for them' (a source of tranquility), not 'send salutations upon them'.

A non-Ahl-al-Bayt person may eat the meat of a sadaqah or vow (nadhr) goat; for an 'aqiqah its bones must not be broken and the breastfeeding mother of the child must not eat it (it reaches the impermissible child via her milk); and one may not eat the meat of an obligatory Hajj sacrifice but may eat that of a voluntary one.

It is a rare exceptional (istisna') case that a man becomes a woman or a woman becomes a man across cycles (karrat); this is no degradation but a high rank, as Sayyidna Sulayman bin Hasan is said to become Mawlatuna Zaynab in later cycles.
Al-kamal al-awwal (the first perfection) is the equal, deficiency-free state in which every intellect was originated, given knowledge, life, and power in one single identical state.
Ibda' (origination) happened only once, producing the mubda'at (originated beings), whereas later creation by the Tenth Intellect is called takhliq.
The giver (mu'ti) of the first perfection is the Mabda' Ta'ala Himself.

Al-kamal al-thani (the second perfection) is greater than the first; its giver is a quality born from the beings' own essences (dhawat) through their own effort and preparation, even though the ultimate bestower remains the Mabda'.
A believer-child is born in the state of the first perfection and attains the second perfection when he takes the 'ahd sharif (sacred covenant).

The second perfection is also called wujud al-thani (the second existence), by which the originated essences attained 'azaliyyah (eternity) and complete 'ismah (infallibility), safe from istihala (transformation) and fana' (annihilation).
The Quran's 'yaf'aluna ma yu'marun wa la ya'sun' establishes that the angels do what they are commanded and never disobey or sin.
A vast uncountable number of originated forms (suwar ibda'iyyah) delayed responding to the call and fell behind, following the Tenth Intellect ('Ashir) in his takhalluf.
The intellects above the Tenth, from the ninth up to the inbi'ath al-awwal, through whose intercession (shafa'a) the 'Ashir's repentance was accepted, are called the kalimat (words).
The 'Ashir is the spiritual Adam (Adam al-ruhani), so the Quranic verse 'fa-talaqqa Adam min rabbihi kalimatin fa-taba 'alayhi' applies to him.

The 'Ashir was commanded to turn to his followers (muqtadin) and call them to salvation, on the principle 'man kasara 'azman fa-'alayhi jabruh' (whoever breaks a bone must mend it), which became a proverb.
The Quranic 'law kunta fazzan ghaliz al-qalbi lanfaddu min hawlik' shows the Messenger's gentleness, which all these qualities of compassion in calling were born within him.

The 'Ashir confessed his error as leaving the recognition of the merit of the predecessor ('alam al-muba'ith al-awwal), repented, and urged his followers to repent so they would be fortunate and successful.
The Prophet's saying 'Qulu la ilaha illa Allah, tuflihu' (Say there is no god but Allah and you will be successful) parallels the 'Ashir's call to the fallen to repent.

The followers rejected all merit ('la fadla lahum 'alayna wa-la laka'), arguing 'kulluna ibda' al-Mabda'' and 'abda'ana sawa'an sawa'' — denying the merit of the prior intellects, the Mabda', and the 'Ashir.

The followers' error was looking only at the equal state of the first perfection and refusing to acknowledge the progress attained in the second perfection — like a person dismissing another's spiritual rank by recalling his childhood.

When the fallen insisted on their claim of equality, their essences darkened (azlamat dhawatuhum) after being luminous, they became estranged from the darkness and entangled with one another, becoming the First Matter (al-hayula al-ula).

Three successive movements of the fallen essences produced first length (al-tul al-awwal), then first width (al-'ard al-awwal), then first depth (al-'umq al-awwal), until they became one body (jism wahid) intermingled together.

The reversal of the movements was from the wisdom of the 'Ashir, who was the mutawalli (manager) responsible for governing the disobedient group and arranged for them an abode (dar), instruments (alat), and a call to salvation.

The disobedient varied in their inner intentions and fell into three categories: the repentant seekers of forgiveness (nadim mustaghfir), the doubting bewildered (shakk mutahayyir), and the insistent arrogant (musirr mustakbir).
Sayyidna Isma'il ibn Hibatullah al-Makrami (Da'i al-Shumukh) in his book al-Kawakib al-Durriyyah explained that the hayula divided into 70 parts: 15 repentant, 20 doubters, and 35 insistent.

The recurrence of 70 in tasbihat (e.g. reciting 'Ya Karimu ya Rahimu ya 'Azim, ya ghiyath al-mustaghithin' seventy times) corresponds to the 70 sections of the hayula, and the ghiyath al-mustaghithin invoked is the 'Ashir al-Mudabbir.

The repentant group was noble and did not blame the 'Ashir; they praised and glorified him as they descended, ending with 'al-hamdu lillahi rabb al-'alamin' — where the Lord of the worlds refers to the 'Ashir al-Mudabbir — so their return (raj'at) happened quickly.
The Prophet's ummah dividing into 73 sects corresponds to the 70 sections plus three (the most severe insistent, the most severe doubter, and the purest repentant).

The post-fard tasbih (Allahu Akbar, Alhamdulillah, Subhanallah 33 times each, ending with La ilaha illa Allah) symbolizes the namiya, hissiyya, and natiqa faculties with the noble form, or the Imam's nasut tabi'i, nasut dhilli, nasut khass with his sura sharif.

The tasbih of the sunnat al-fajr ('Subhana rabbi al-'azim wa-bi-hamdihi, astaghfirullah al-'azim wa-atubu ilayh') is the very tasbih the repentant seekers of forgiveness (nadimin mustaghfirin) recited as they fell.
The munajat of the istiftah ('ya rabbi zalamtu nafsi fa-ghfir li... la yaghfiru al-dhanb al-'azim illa anta ya 'Aliyyu ya 'Azim') is from Imam Husayn ibn 'Ali.

Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq narrated that the Lord asks the angels what His servants say in their prostration, and upon hearing they confess wronging their souls and seek His forgiveness, He makes the angels witnesses that He has forgiven and pardoned them.
Allah forgives all sins ('Inna Allah yaghfiru al-dhunub jami'an', 'La taqnatu min rahmat Allah') except shirk, which the Quran calls al-zulm al-'azim.

The 'illa anta' that alone forgives the great sin refers to the Imam of the time, ultimately the 'ayn al-akhirah — the Qa'im 'ala dhikrihi al-salam — who holds the jami'iyyat of 400,000 years (seven satr and seven kashf) and is the qasim al-nar wa-l-jannah (divider of Fire and Garden).
Mawlana 'Ali is also called qasim al-nar wa-l-jannah in a partial sense.
At the gate of paradise people will be stopped and questioned about the walayat of 'Ali — a question on which the great Sunni scholars and all Shia agree.
The forms (suwar) of a believer across successive cycles unite and merge with the later forms, so souls progress across cycles toward settlement.

Yunus, sahib al-hut, said 'la ilaha illa anta, subhanaka inni kuntu min al-zalimin' — combining tawhid, tasbih, and istighfar — and 'la ilaha illa anta' appears only once in the Quran, of greater status than all other forms, directed toward the 'ayn al-'azimah.
Yunus did his tasbih for 40 days, and had he not done it he would have remained in the fish until the Day of Resurrection (yawm yub'athun).
The number 40 carries a power of maturity: a person reaches maturity at 40, the Prophet was made a messenger at age 40, and if 40 people gather and pray for someone their prayer is accepted.

'Umar ibn al-Khattab was the 40th person to accept Islam, upon which the Messenger said Islam had gained strength — likened (per Qutb al-Din) to a house declared built once its final part is completed.

From the 'Ashir's (the Mover's) first motion of the hayula were created the awtad al-falak (pegs of the spheres), four non-visible constellations: tali' (ascendant, east), gharib (descendant, west), 'ashir (mid-sky), and rabi' (under the earth).

When the density overflowed, the four awtad and the two poles (qutba al-falak from north and south) pulled it and held it in the middle of the sphere, the falak encompassing it from all sides like the white and shell encompass an egg's yolk.
The atmosphere split and the spheres were arranged into nine, each sphere contained within the one after it like the layers of an onion.
The falak al-muhit (encompassing sphere) surrounds all spheres and moves them every day and night with one total divine motion by the governing power of the mudabbir, from east to west.

There are seven spheres from Zuhal (Saturn) down to the moon, and all stars reside in the eighth sphere, named the falak al-buruj (sphere of constellations) — just as all believers ultimately gather at the Bab al-Abwab.
The falak al-buruj is divided into twelve constellations (buruj), each with 30 houses, totaling 360 degrees.
The spiritual essences (fudala) ascend through all 360 degrees of the zodiac for purification, traversing them in roughly 720 years of going and coming plus 280 years.

The Quran's 'wa lakum fi al-qisasi hayatun ya uli al-albab' means our very life runs within the vast circle of qisas (retribution), spread across many cycles, not merely that retribution occurs within our life.
The ninth sphere (falak al-muhit) is empty of constellations and planets due to its subtlety and nobility — just as no form gathers with the 'Aql al-Awwal / Mubda' al-Awwal in the spiritual realm.

Two du'at gave two counts of the intellects collected at the Mubda' al-Awwal: Sayyidna 'Ali bin Sulayman said 28 (seeing the 'uqul in totality), Sayyidna Hasan bin Nuh said 12 (the letters of 'La ilaha illa Allah') — both are correct, differing only in perspective.
The Imam takes the forms (suwarat) but the Mubda' al-Awwal does not take them; the governing decisions are made by the 'Aql al-Awwal even though the forms gather at the Mubda' al-Awwal.
When the Imam hands the gathered collection of forms (the imamat) to his farzand, the farzand — previously an Imam in potential made of riya' — goes from potential to actual.

Upon the Imam's passing the Bab al-Abwab also passes away and becomes the heart (qalb) of the Imam's farzand; this is illustrated by the death of Mawlana Abu Talib (the Imam) followed three days later by Khadija (his hujjat) in the Prophet's Year of Grief.
Mawlatuna Khadija is the Bab al-Abwab of Bibi Fatimah al-Zahra.

When the spheres cast their rays toward the earth, something of their nature returned to their essences and shells (asdaf) formed upon the non-visible spheres, rendering the stars visible but introducing negativity (nahusat) — so Zuhal, pure in essence, acquired inauspiciousness through its sadaf.

The stars in their original state were notional (wahmiyya) and invisible like the spheres; the Mudabbir made the asdaf by His wisdom so they would be perceptible and illuminate the dark physical world.

At the 'Ashir's call the fallen disobeyed saying 'la nasma'u wa la nuti'', accepting only the Mabda' Ta'ala and claiming equality (sawa'an bi-sawa'), thereby acknowledging only the first perfection while denying the second perfection attained by the intellects and the Mubda' al-Awwal.
Isbagh al-wudu' is performing ablution thoroughly three times; there is no established virtue (la fadila lahu) in doing it beyond the third, though one praying alone is not forbidden from more.
One leading prayer must not prolong tasbihat or recite long surahs, as weak or weary followers cannot bear it.
Density (kathafa) brings a being down while subtlety (latafa) raises it; spiritual progress is attained through subtlety, and the hayula fell from the realm of purity due to density.

The 'Ashir arranged the physical world by rank of purity: the seven spheres and planets from the purest (the repentant nadimin), the four mothers (fire, air, water, earth) from the middling (the doubters and bewildered), and the sakhra (core of the earth) from the densest (the insistent and arrogant).

The falak al-muhit, encompassing the entire realm, is called the gate of the spiritual world ('alam al-quds); beyond it lies first the world of life ('alam al-hayat), not directly the spiritual world.

Of those who repented with the 'Ashir's repentance, the group 'Ta'ibu bi-Tawbatihi' ascended as intellects with his group, while another group ('Labbu Nida'ahu', who answered his call) had a separate world of life created for them, containing the tamur (repository) and the spiritual Ka'ba connected to the physical Ka'ba.

The 'alam al-niyyat (world of intention) is the upper realm of our intentions at origination; after origination we remained passive, not joining the intellects who affirmed God's oneness, until we fell into the 'Ashir's illusory equality, and there our world of intention was established by our differing consciences.
The tamur, above the falak al-muhit in the world of life, holds the original essences of the mohtajibin (the veiled ones of the Imams) who did not enter the spiritual world.
The Prophet's mi'raj (ascension) reached only the falak al-muhit and then returned, because beyond it one cannot return without becoming an intellect.

The twelve constellations of the falak al-buruj are: Hamal (Aries), al-Thawr (Taurus), al-Jawza' (Gemini), al-Sartan (Cancer), al-Asad (Leo), al-Sunbula (Virgo), al-Mizan (Libra), al-'Aqrab (Scorpio), al-Qaws (Sagittarius), al-Jady (Capricorn), al-Dalw (Aquarius), and al-Hut (Pisces).

The seven planetary spheres in order are Zuhal (Saturn), Mushtari (Jupiter), Mirrikh (Mars), Shams (Sun), Zuhra (Venus), 'Utarid (Mercury), and Qamar (Moon); from their revolutions arose the spheres of ether and air (kurra-e-asir, kurra-e-nasim) and the four mothers.

The governing being assigned the planets to administer the physical world in sequence under Zuhal's overall governance (Mushtari, Mirrikh, Shams, Zuhra, 'Utarid as helpers), and in the seventh thousand-year period the first human came into being under Qamar's partnership.
The spheres revolve around the earth (with the Ka'ba as center point), not around the sun; modern science has changed its position on this three times.

The Mudabbir Ta'ala made the opposites (azdad) of the celestial bodies by His wisdom to illuminate the dark physical world, and the senses perceiving them confirms the power of the Planner and the soundness of the celestial world.
When the falak al-muhit moved, the atmosphere below the moon's sphere reached extreme heat and dryness — the nature of fire — and was named asir (ether), the first of the four mothers.

Every sphere has its own kawkab except the falak al-muhit and the falak al-buruj; the falak al-muhit is invisible (ghair-mar'i) and its single 24-hour total motion, called the divine motion, drives all the spheres and planets below it.

After death a person is divided into three: the surat-e-sharif goes instantly to its hadd-e-'ali on earth; the middle part (riyat), released after three days, goes to the spheres (mainly the moon's, also Jupiter and the Sun) to be refined; and the body's purification proceeds to the falak al-buruj over 360 years.
The body's purification journey through the zodiac takes 720 years ascending and descending plus 280 years, returning after 1000 years minus its namiya, hissiya, and natiqa faculties.
In one kaur (cycle) a believer's fuzlah repeats 360 times, and Sayyidna 'Ali wrote that a believer's body contains 360 nufus, each of which progresses each cycle by becoming a nafs.

If a believer's hadd-e-'ali has passed away with a good end, his form merges (muwazajat) with it; if the hadd-e-'ali is still alive, his form remains in the vicinity (jiwar) — guarding against loss should the hadd-e-'ali go astray.
If a hadd-e-'ali goes astray, the ascending one's form is removed and he is given another hadd-e-'ali.

When one who served the da'wat goes astray, his luminous form (surat-e-nayyirah) earned by his good deeds is separated from his bad form — as Da'ud ibn Qutb's noble form passed to Sayyidna Muhammad ibn Fu'ad, and Abu Bakr's luminous form (from his service to the Prophet) passed to his son Muhammad bin Abi Bakr.
One's hadd-e-'ali must be from the current Imam's hudud, never from the ranks of a previous Imam whose cycle (haikal) is over.

Promotion cannot be held back; a lower one (adna) cannot restrain his higher one, and if a hadd-e-'ali is promoted into the gathering assembly the lower one is simply assigned a replacement hadd-e-'ali.
In the daur-e-kashf returns occur every thousand years, but the people of the daur-e-qa'im (the final era, like us) return first and are not bound by the thousand-year rule.
A believer has only one hadd-e-'ali, but a hadd-e-'ali may have a whole congregation (majma') of believers.
The Prophet said that when a believer prays, two rows pray behind him — his unseen (ghair-mar'i) congregation of his hadd-e-'ali.
When a questioner asks a question he is often a medium through whom a form from his congregation, or his hadd-e-'ali, asks for its own satisfaction of knowledge.

The Quran's 'Innal-hasanati yudhhibnas-sayyi'at' means the believer's hasanat — his lower ranks (hudud-e-daniya), still engaged in tasbih and pursuit of knowledge — eliminate his evil deeds, namely the doubts and misgivings (shukuk wa shubhat) in his hadd-e-'ali.
Doubt is necessary for a believer because the plant of certainty (yaqin) always grows in the soil of doubt (shakk).

Ibrahim's request to see how the dead are revived ('li-yatma'inna qalbi') shows that certainty is above faith ('al-yaqinu fawqa al-iman'); his belief was iman, but the satisfaction of the heart he sought was yaqin.

A hadd-e-'ali is appointed only after one takes the 'ahd-e-sharif, which is the spiritual birth (wiladat-e-batini) as distinct from the physical birth (wiladat-e-zahiri); before it one cannot have a hadd-e-'ali or become a hadd (zimmah) for others, lacking the magnet to attract the iron.

The four mothers form in sequence by the spheres' diminishing motion: asir (ether, center of fire, invisible, its light concealed by divine wisdom), hawa (air, moderate), ma' (water, cold and flowing), and earth (extreme cold and dryness).
The Mudabbir willed the earth to be the place for the appearance of the mawalid (creations): mineral (ma'dan), vegetable (nabat), animal (hayawan), and human (the rational animal, hayawan-e-natiq).

The celestial rays struck the hard rock (sakhra), recoiled from its hardness, returned reflected and heated the earth's surface and air, producing nasim (the breeze, center of water) and zamharir (intense cold, the highest part of the nasim sphere).

The sun's opposite (sadaf/azdad), like all the celestial bodies', was formed from the rock mixture; the kawakib are noble in essence (made of the highest parts of the nadimin) but their azdad acquired inauspiciousness from the rock, which is the basis of planetary effects on people.
The markaz al-ma' (center of water) is not water itself; if one travels there, water is not present — it is only the center from which water is balanced.
The Quran's 'Wa-llahu anbatakum min al-ardi nabata' establishes two kinds of human creation: from the earth (more excellent and higher) and from spiritual parents (lower).

Resurrection is true ('innal-ba'tha haqqun') and is of two kinds: the believer's resurrection (raised in faith after dying in faith) and the Prophet's resurrection at the praised station (maqam mahmud), appearing from Quds, into which Salman al-Farsi entered first and then the Prophet.
A qutb is born at the beginning of every cycle; the qutb of this cycle was born in Sarandib, and the qutb of the very first cycle of the du'at was born in the Ka'ba — the place where 'Ali was born.
The Quran's 'wa anzalna al-hadid fihi ba'sun shadid' states iron was sent down from the sky, and reciting this verse on Tuesday has great virtue.

The two nodes (head and tail, ra's wa dhanab) lie beyond the moon's sphere, the tail more severe than the head; the evil concepts (tasawwur-e-qabih) of the opposites of the du'at, prophets, and nuqata' went to the head, and those of the Imams, hujjats, and awsiya went to the tail.
The Mudabbir ('Ashir al-Mudabbir) delegated the administration of the world to Zuhal (Saturn) by his own substance, and Zuhal administers for a thousand years.

From the intermingled natures arose vapors, dense clouds, and continuous non-beneficial rains (matar al-su', the evil rain mentioned in the Quran), which carry impurities down, whereas good rains bring down the purified luminous essences (fudulat-e-nayyirah) from the falak al-buruj.

The essence's purification journey runs from the first degree of the first zodiac to the last and back, 720 years total; the book being read (Sayyidna Mu'ayyad al-Shirazi's) supplies the Tahajjud du'a 'la tuksiranna ya Rabbi fi hadha al-safarana' (do not prolong our journey).

Spiritual progress moves from the physical world to the psychic world: the body becomes a nafs (namiya, hissiya, natiqa), reaches the station of the sura, then the station of the 'aql (intellect) on some distant day (yawman ma); once the form enters the Imam's haykal it is like a fixed deposit that progresses with the Imam.
