The mizaj-e-muntazij of essences is ascending through vapors (bukharat) and descending through rainwater after purification.

Even unbelievers, infidels, and hypocrites return after 1000 years; after purification they reach the station of affirmations (ta'yidat) with a thousand-year lifespan, becoming in actuality the angels they were in potentiality.
Per Sayyidna 'Ali, of five times one is when prayers are accepted, namely 'inda nuzul al-ghayth (at the time of rainfall), because at that time the purified essences are descending and ascending.

When the people asked the Messenger to pray for rain and then for it to stop, he recited 'khuliqa al-insanu min 'ajal' (man was created of haste); a parallel rain miracle occurred in the time of Sayyidna Ghulam Husain at Gandipet, traced back through Sayyidna 'Ali bin Qutbuddin (author of Bahrat al-'Adillah) and Sayyidna Isma'il bin Hibatullah.

At his death Sayyidna Mu'ayyad al-Shirazi wept, saying 'mata yalhaku al-baytu ila rabbihi' (when will the house join its Lord) — the body (house) longing to join its noble form (Lord) — before his four student-du'at including Lamak bin Malik.

The principle 'al-mu'minu yanzuru bi-nurillah' (the believer sees with the light of God) was invoked by Sayyidna Ja'far regarding the 12-year-old Sayyidna Hasan Khan, foreseeing 'yakunu lahu sha'nun min sha'n' (he will have a great station); Hasan Khan later wrote 70 books in haqa'iq.

In Zuhal's first thousand years the earth became a surging sea ('Wa sarat al-ardu bahran muwwajan') and fermented essences (khama'ir) resembling Saturn's nature — iron, stone, copper, and the Sudanese, farmers (zarra'a), the wretched (ahl al-shaqa), and the harsh — were formed.

Mushtari (Jupiter) is the Sa'd-e-Akbar; Jupiter and Venus are the two auspicious planets (sa'dayn), and 'al-Mushtari bayna al-nahsayn' (Jupiter between the two inauspicious) is illustrated by the Prophet's grave lying between Abu Bakr and 'Umar.

The 14-rak'at prayer at the Prophet's Mosque is offered at the pillars (ras, maqam al-Tawbah, Hannanah, 'Ali, etc.), of which the eight rak'at at the pillars are most meritorious, alluding to the bearers of the Throne; the maqam al-Tawbah is the spot the Prophet said people would draw lots for if they knew its virtue.

The successive thousand-year planetary governances each fermented essences of matching nature: Mushtari (pious religious people, vegetation, crawling creatures), Mirrikh (commanders, soldiers, minerals), Shams (kings, ruby, gold), Zuhra (Arabs, women, singers, fruits, birds), and 'Utarid (scribes, ministers, accountants), preparing for the human's appearance in the seventh millennium.

The human person appeared in the seventh thousand years 'nabatan min al-ardi' (as a plant from the earth), per 'wa-Allahu anbatakum min al-ardi nabata'; dinosaurs and similar claims of science have no mention in this tradition and are fiction.

A hadd is a fixed limit or measurement, per the Quran's 'la ta'tadu hudud Allah... man yata'adda hudud Allahi faqad zalama nafsahu' (do not transgress Allah's limits; whoever does has wronged himself).

When a believer dies his namiya, hissiya, and natiqa souls instantly unite into the surah sharifah, which goes to its hadd-e-'ali — one superior to it in rank by only a nineteen-to-twenty difference, not a da'i or hujjat of the time.

The Tahiyyat al-Masjid's mamsulat (referents) include one's hadd-e-'ali and its hadd-e-'ali; as a gift to the mosque it requires reciting the descending surahs (Falaq then Nas), a practice otherwise reserved for obligatory prayers and the sunnah of fajr, giving it special status.
A living hadd-e-'ali does not stop the lower one's wrong deeds, but a knowledge-loving hadd-dani can incite his hadd-e-'ali toward the world of knowledge if the latter is disinclined to it.

The 'ahd-e-sharif is the greatest act of worship, surpassing obligatory prayers, Hajj, Zakat, and fasting; without it the surah sharif is never formed and no hadd-e-'ali can be appointed, so it is renewed yearly on Yawm al-Ghadir per 'wa-dhakkir fa-inna al-dhikra tanfa'u al-mu'minin'.

Through the 'ahd-e-sharif one receives a nuqta-e-nur (point of light) from one's own hadd in the spiritual world, from its inabat and tawbah, per the Quran's 'la tansa nasibaka min al-dunya' — meaning do not die without the 'ahd-e-sharif.

A minimal 'ahd-e-sharif can be completed in one's last moments by taking the name of the Imam of the time and sending blessings upon him; even loving and obeying the infallible Imam of the time (khalifat Allah fi al-ard) without a formal covenant is tremendously beneficial.

Children who die young (ahl-e-istighar) do not have a surah formed, but have a majma'-e-sighar that progresses; this assembly was first given to Bibi Fatimah al-Zahra then to Mawlana Baqir, and the children of the A'imma who die young form the majma'-e-mufritin, also under Bibi Fatimah's care.

The believer's journey after death proceeds from higher hudud to the Bab al-Abwab; when the haykal gathered there is complete, the Imam acquires it and hands it to his farzand, who thereby goes from Imam in potential to Imam in actuality.

The Imam hands the gathered majma' to his farzand in four days or four years; rarely Mawlana 'Abd al-Muttalib received the majma' before birth, so his mother said 'wulidtu shaybah' (I gave birth to an old man) because his hair was white.
The spiritual majma' of nasut and lahut runs completely parallel (mumathil) to the nasut: a rank attained in nasut corresponds exactly to the form's place in lahut, never higher or lower.

Animals that die their own death in the 6000 years died a halal death, like the pigeons of the Ka'ba and Madinah, which cannot be hunted yet die halal because they are formed from the fudlat of the mukasirin.

A mukasir is the da'wat teacher who breaks (kasr) his students' false beliefs and establishes correct belief through his hujjat; he carries the entire load of the da'wat from the Imam down to the lowest rank, like the feet bearing the body's weight.

As reward for their lifelong labor, jewels (jawahir), rubies (yawaqit), and salt form from the fudlat and bones of the mukasirin; the Prophet said 'al-milh qabl al-ta'am wa ba'd al-ta'am yaqta'u sab'ina da'an, awwaluha al-junun wa al-juzam' (salt before and after food wards off seventy diseases, the least being madness and leprosy).

The Quran's 'fas'alu ahl al-dhikr in kuntum la ta'lamun', per Imam Husayn, means the Ahl al-Bayt are the ahl al-dhikr; God divided the world into ahl al-dhikr and la ta'lamun, obliging the latter to ask, but not obliging the Ahl al-Bayt to answer.

In the seventh millennium the higher governor moved the sphere and vapors ascended from the dregs of minerals, plants, and animals, became clouds (ghuyum), and poured down as a pure rain ('amtaran safiyatan') that made shallow furrows (khudad) in the earth.

A second, nobler vapor rose from the furrows and poured down as rain 'shabihatun bi-maniy al-rajul' (like a man's semen) into the furrows 'shabihatun bi-arham al-nisa'' (like women's wombs), mixed with the woman-like water, and took form through the stages of creation over nine months by the Mudabbir's arrangement and the celestial bodies' influence.

After nine months the first human opened his eyes, inhaled the nasim, rolled in and absorbed the remaining oily water through his pores, was nourished first from his navel then sucked his thumb (from which his Creator caused pure milk to flow), explaining infants' thumb-sucking habit.
The first human spent nine months plus one full year in the pit, then stood up the size of a four-year-old child due to the greatness of his parents, who are the heaven and the earth.

The Imam has four things: his nasut, his lahut, his nafs, and his surah; in the obligatory four-rak'at prayer the higher first two rak'at allude to the Imam's nafs and surah sharif, the latter two to his nasut and lahut.

The Imam's nasut is made from the riya' of the believers and the hudud of the da'wat, and his lahut from their surat; both are borrowed, only the Imam's nafs and surah being his own, which is why celestial bodies and poison can affect his borrowed body.

The Imam's nafs-e-hissiyah is so exalted it bears all the nawasit, lawahiq, lahut, and nasut of the entire era; Amir al-Mu'minin 'Ali ibn Abi Talib's nafs-e-hissiyah carried the hayakil of all the A'imma from Hunays to Abu al-Qayyim.

The Imam is infallible, so 'Ali uprooting the gate of Khaybar 'la bi-quwwatin jismaniyyatin bal bi-quwwatin ruhaniyyah/rabbaniyyah' was an allusion to the strength granted by his muhtajib (veiled one), not physical strength.
The Imam, being infallible, fulfills our qisasat; any difficulty falls upon the riya' and the believers, not upon him, his original essence remaining far removed.
'Ali's words at the blow ('fuztu bi-Rabb al-Ka'bah') related to the qisasat; 'Ali was the bearer of the surat of 10,000 years (plus 3,000 years of fatrat).

The present Amir holds the jami'iyyat of 400,000 surat (seven daur-e-kashf and six daur-e-satr) in his seventh manifestation; he is the khalifah of the Qayyim, the Qayyim the khalifah of the 'Ashir, and while the Amir is the 'ayn-e-awwalah the Qayyim is the 'ayn-e-akhirah.

In each pit (khudad) males were created first and females afterward from the remaining water; multiple pits were created at Sarandib and across the 12 islands, including evil pits from which enemies and adversaries arose.
There is a city in Sarandib named Nur Eliya, said to be the manifestation (tajalli) of Mawlana 'Ali.
The Exalted Planner (al-mudabbir ta'ala) separated and distinguished the purest, noblest, most excellent, and most subtle part of the rainwater descending from the sky.
The purest portion of the rain was carried to the noblest of places (ashraf al-biqa'), which in the first epoch was Sarandib because it was the locus of earthly equilibrium (mawda' i'tidal al-ard).
Twenty-eight individuals were formed in the depressions (al-qudad) of Sarandib, who in honor, purity, and excellence surpassed all other humans, with the rank of the red ruby over ordinary stone.
Amir al-Mu'minin ('Ali) declared 'I am the red ruby' (anal-yaqut al-ahmar) and that the Messenger of Allah is the yellow ruby (al-yaqut al-asfar).

Among the twenty-eight, one individual (the jussa ibda'iyah) is superior to all in nobility and excellence, like the red ruby over a stone, and he is the essence (zubdah), choicest part (safwa), and extract (khulasa) of the world.
The one individual attained superiority over the other twenty-seven because of his purity of intention (safa' an-niyyah) and his great remorse (kathrat an-nadam) for his fault at the call of 'Ashir.
When the noble individual emerged from the depressions, he looked at his own essence by his own essence, without any teacher (mu'allim) or inspirer (mulhim), and contemplated the world.

Contemplating the constructed sky, the spread-out earth, and the varied creatures, the noble individual reasoned that he, his species, and the whole world have a single Creator (mubdi') who is different from them.
The noble individual negated divinity (ilahiyyah) from himself and all creatures and affirmed it for his Creator, bearing witness to Him.
The power to bring from non-existence (nist) into existence (hast) is not in any creature; this is a skill belonging only to the rank of the first intellect.
The noble individual stood in the lower world (al-'alam ad-dani) at the station of the First Precedent (maqam as-sabiq al-awwal), mirroring the station of 'aql al-awwal in the spiritual world.

Once his intellect became pure, his portion of substance (maddah) and support (ta'id) connected with him, establishing the principle that anyone with a pure intellect and clean thought necessarily receives divine support.

Even though the ibda'iyah were born knowing their own status, the Imams, like other creatures, must still acquire knowledge and study, as the Quran states they were brought forth from their mothers' wombs knowing nothing, while remaining infallible (ma'sum) from the beginning.
The jussa ibda'iyah gathered the twenty-seven individuals, from whom his physical form (haykal) was prepared, and from this the purification of the world (takhlis al-'alam) occurred.

The son of the jussa ibda'iyah was the first Imam; the imamat began with him and will continue in his lineage until the Day of Resurrection through every epoch (dawr al-kashf, dawr al-sitr, dawr al-fatrah).
The twenty-seven individuals are not ordinary; they are the essence (zubdah) and cream of creation, superior to those born naturally.

The jussa ibda'iyah received substance and support not directly but at the hands of the First Precedent (sabiq al-awwal) through the intermediary of all the creative intellects (al-'uqul al-ibda'iyah).

Through that substance the jussa ibda'iyah was ennobled and came to know what was and what will be (ma kana wa ma sayakun), as had been granted to 'aql al-awwal, muba'ath as-sabil, and the creative intellects.

The noble individual then called the twenty-seven who were with him to affirm Allah and His Oneness (wahdaniyyah), acknowledge His divinity, and negate divinity from themselves, and all of them responded with 'labbayk'.
Unlike the spiritual world where some denied 'Ashir, in the lower world all twenty-seven affirmed and brought faith, denying divinity for themselves and acknowledging Allah as Creator.
The Quranic verse 'shahidallahu annahu la ilaha illa huwa' is interpreted such that the name Allah is applied to 'aql al-awwal and 'huwa' (He) refers to the mubdi' ta'ala.

'Aql al-awwal could not name the mubdi' ta'ala and so gestured and said 'huwa' (He); Sayyidna al-Mu'ayyad said even saying 'huwa' is a sin accompanied by seeking forgiveness (dhambun mashfu'un bil-istighfar).

The angels (al-mala'ikah) who bore witness in the verse are the incorporeal intellects (al-'uqul al-mujarradah), the nine intellects from the second to the tenth, who hastened to the call made through muba'ath as-sabil.
'Aql al-awwal did not himself make a call; the call happened through muba'ath as-sabil, otherwise a circle of gathered intellects would have formed around 'aql al-awwal.
The people of knowledge (ulul-'ilm) in the verse are the noble individual (sahib jussa ibda'iyah) together with his twenty-seven hudud who respond to and bear witness to his call.
They are alluded to as 'people of knowledge' because they are the repository (mahill) of substances and supports, which is intellectual knowledge ('ilm al-'aqli) given to support them.
Among the twenty-seven, ranks are established according to each one's purity (safa) and response (ijabah); they are not of one rank but hold distinct ranks in repentance, gnosis, and testimony.
Just as the companions held different ranks, with the Imam the hujjatul layl and hujjatul nahar have different ranks, and the Imam chooses among them.
The hujjatul layl, who are always in the Imam's presence, are superior to the hujjatul nahar.
The bab al-zahir and bab al-batin are from among the twelve.
In the Imam's presence are the bab al-imbi'as; the bab al-batin is superior, and the bab al-imbi'as is even superior to the bab al-batin.

The verse 'shahidallahu annahu la ilaha illa huwa wal-mala'ikatu wa ulul-'ilmi qa'iman bil-qist, la ilaha illa huwa al-'aziz al-hakim' is a very special verse in which the kalimah shahadah appears twice.
The kalimah la ilaha illallah appears in the Quran in five intonations: la ilaha illallah, la ilaha illa huwa, la ilaha illa ana, la ilaha illalladhi, and la ilaha illa anta.

There are thirty-seven such kalimat of testimony in the Quran appearing across thirty-six verses, since one verse (shahidallah) contains it twice, giving that verse great importance and a tasbih of great power.
The Da'i 'Abd al-'Ali (al-Wazir) wrote that whoever recites these thirty-six verses has his prayer accepted immediately, as mentioned in Majmu' al-Ad'iyah.

A tradition of Qadi Shurayh states that whoever recites these verses will attain ten states; Qadi Shurayh lost his eyesight and regained it by reciting the kalimah shahadah intonations in order on the Prophet's instruction.
This entire verse is included in the kalimat at-tahlil (verses of tahlil) recited in the community's prayer.

The moon, the last intellect of the kawr, assisted Jupiter (Zuhal) in administration for a thousand years, which was a thousand years of felicity and the establishment of the Noble Mission (da'wah sharifah).
The da'wah sharif is not the name of a room or chamber but, in the spiritual world, the name of the intellects, and in the physical world, the name of the assembly formed by these hudud.

The noble individual (jussa ibda'iyah) separated the twenty-seven and sent them to the twelve islands (ithna 'ashar jazirah) of the earth to call people to the worship and obedience of Allah and to teach them.
Those called were the jussas born in the islands, of whom many were born in different places.
They taught the people the knowledge of worldly life ('ilm al-ma'ash) and the knowledge of the Hereafter ('ilm al-ma'ad).

The noble individual taught each da'i the language of the people to whom he was sent, since every island had its own language, fulfilling the verse 'We have not sent any messenger except in the language of his people'.

teaching: Without revelation (wahy) and connected support (ta'id), the noble individual could not have taught the properties, benefits, harms, beneficial medicines, and deadly poisons of minerals, plants, and animals from himself.

This teaching of properties verifies the Quranic statement 'And He taught Adam all the names' (wa 'allama Adama al-asma'a kullaha), because the noble individual is the First Adam (al-Adam al-awwal) and the Father of Humanity (Abu al-Bashar).
'Ashir is the spiritual Adam, while the jussa ibda'iyah is the First Adam of the physical world and the father (teacher) of his species in worldly and otherworldly matters.
Had Allah's grace not supported the noble individual, by which he was made deserving through his glorification (tasbih) and administration (tadbir) for his Lord, all the people would have perished.

The punishment of the accursed ones lasts for one kawr, but some are taken out earlier due to their just deserts (mujibat-i-'adliyah), emerging through volcanic lava and then returning in human form via the plants that grow.
Umar bin 'Abd al-'Aziz was taken out of punishment before his time as reward for stopping the cursing of 'Ali from seventy thousand pulpits and returning the garden of Fadak to the Ahl al-Bayt.
Souls return in human form even where only infidels eat the plants grown from volcanic lava; after repentance is accepted (tawba 'alayh) they gradually move into other cycles.
The human form is a common platform from which souls both fall and climb.

Each da'i in his island taught the people how to make clothes from trees, obtain food from minerals and animals, and the way of salvation through the worship and obedience of Allah and obedience to His chosen wali (the Imam of the time) on earth.

The noble individual established in his presence at Sarandib twelve individuals who are the Hujjatul Layl (Proofs of the Night), the most excellent, associated with the Night Prayer (Salat al-Layl), in which twelve rak'at are prayed at once.

The hujjatul layl are kept together in the Imam's presence, while the hujjatun nahar are stationed in separate islands, paired such that two hujjatun nahar of a da'i are tied to another da'i, one higher and one lower, reflected in praying two rak'at at a time.
The Tahajjud is for the hujjatun nahar, and the concluding du'a is for the Da'wat — a call to the twelve hujjatul layl to join Qa'im Al-i-Islam or the Imam of the time.
Among the twelve hujjatul layl, four are called the Khurum and are more excellent than the other eight; the twelve themselves are more excellent than the twenty-seven born with the jussa.
Among the four Khurum, one is superior and is the Bab (gate) of that noble station (the Imam or the jussa ibda'iyah himself).
The term station (maqam) applies to three persons: the Imam, the Wasi, and the Nabi.
The noble individual appointed before each da'i in his island three persons: a Mukasir, a Ma'dhun Mutlaq, and a Da'i Mahsur.
These ranks (Mukasir, Ma'dhun, Da'i) are preserved (mahfuzah) and are never cut off with any Natiq, Wasi, or Imam in his epoch.

Every da'i commanded the people of his island that each should marry a woman formed in a cavern other than his own, and not marry the woman who emerged from his own cavern from the remnant of his water, who is like his sister.

From one cavern, males were born first and then females from the remaining water, fulfilling 'Men are the protectors and maintainers of women' (ar-rijalu qawwamuna 'ala an-nisa'); these women were the sisters of those men and unlawful to marry.
This exogamous practice is the pure, unblemished way of the People of Truth (tariq ahl al-haqq).

The exoteric belief (held by the ignorant ahl az-zahir) that Adam married the children of his first wife's womb to those of the second womb is rejected, because it would make all human progeny born of incest/fornication (sifah).
The Du'at affirm the correct account against the ignorant, praising Allah with 'praise be to Allah who guided us to this, and we would not have been guided had Allah not guided us'.
The birth from the earth happened in a single event (daf'ah wahidah) in the first epoch and never recurred, mirroring how the mubdi' ta'ala brought all creations (mubda'at) into existence at once.
After the single earth-birth, all subsequent human births until today occur through procreation (tanasul) between man and woman.
Believing women who are very pure and worship purely for Allah are gradually made men in the coming cycles (karr) due to their worship; such risen women are very few (illa ma sha' Allah).
When a woman rises to a higher state, another is brought to the pit in her place, because women remain a necessity of the world and the ratio is preserved.
Sulayman bin Hasan said of his wife Khadijah bint Nuh, 'kanat hiya dhukur' (she was male), meaning she outwardly wore a woman's dress but was inwardly a man.
